key_headlines.title: National Debt Ratio Illusion amid Super Budget; Semiconductor Downturn Could Be Toxic
key_headlines.summary: Korea faces record fiscal expansion despite national debt expected to rise 22.7% by 2030, with concerns about fiscal sustainability if semiconductor boom falters.

key_headlines.title: Future Home Prices Dependent on Tax Reform and Interest Rates
key_headlines.summary: Real estate experts cite tax system overhaul (55.6%) and base rate hikes (50%) as key factors influencing housing prices, with only 16.7% expecting Seoul stability by next year.

key_headlines.title: Only 1-2 Out of 10 Experts Expect Seoul House Prices to Stabilize Next Year
key_headlines.summary: Half of real estate professionals believe Seoul housing market stabilization will remain difficult in coming months, contradicting government expectations of year-end stabilization.

key_headlines.title: BOK's Final Rate Decision This Month; Growth and Inflation Provide Hints
key_headlines.summary: Bank of Korea scheduled to decide on base rate on November 26, with 2026 growth forecast revised upward to around 3.8% and potential for rate hike amid persistent inflation.

key_headlines.title: Real Estate Tax Reform Criticized for Simultaneous Increase in Holding and Transfer Taxes
key_headlines.summary: National Assembly Budget Office raises concerns that dual tax hikes on property ownership and sales may undermine government's intention to encourage housing market transactions.

sections.Hot Economy News: Korea's economy shows mixed signals with third-quarter GDP growth of 1.0% significantly exceeding expectations, yet consumers struggle with persistent high inflation and rising interest burdens. Consumer prices rose 2.8% year-over-year in October for the second consecutive month, driven by agricultural products, processed foods, and petroleum prices increasing 15%. The Bank of Korea is expected to make its final rate decision of the year on November 26, with potential for additional rate hikes as core inflation remains elevated despite economic growth acceleration.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The government's record fiscal expansion strategy faces scrutiny as national debt is projected to increase 22.7% by 2030, raising concerns about fiscal sustainability if the semiconductor boom reverses. Third-quarter GDP growth reached 1.0%, more than tripling earlier forecasts of 0.3%, driven by export performance and recovery signs. However, the rapid expansion of cash welfare programs and accelerating super-aging demographics are pushing government spending forecasts 80 trillion won higher than initially projected through 2030. Consumer price inflation persists at 2.8%, with the Bank of Korea signaling continued monetary tightening to address inflationary pressures.
sections.Financial Markets: Korean stock markets (KOSPI and KOSDAQ) opened lower on profit-taking concerns despite favorable global conditions including lower oil and interest rates from US-Iran negotiations. The KOSPI fell to the 5,700 level as US midterm election results and employment data expectations create uncertainty about Federal Reserve rate cut prospects. The Korean won-dollar exchange rate stands at 1,342.9 won as of mid-morning, reflecting broader market volatility. New ETF products are being launched, including the ACE Global Memory Semiconductor Top 3 Bond Hybrid Active ETF targeting memory semiconductor companies and domestic bonds in equal proportions.
sections.Industry & Technology: Domestic EV tax credit expansion is gaining bipartisan support in parliament as Chinese electric vehicle market share grows rapidly, with discussions expected in November Finance and Economy Committee. AI, biotech, semiconductor, and robotics companies are attracting talent through major job fairs, with DGIST developing innovative battery-free soft robots powered by external force. South Korean EV makers face competitive pressure, with lawmakers arguing for inclusion in tax benefits similar to the US Inflation Reduction Act to protect domestic industry competitiveness.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul housing market is experiencing temporary stabilization as accumulated inventory and strengthened lending restrictions create a pause, yet 50% of professionals expect continued instability near-term. Gyeonggi Province property prices are being driven by advanced industrial hubs including semiconductor production bases, with top 10 appreciation areas led by Seongnam, Gwangmyeong, and Hanam. Rental market sentiment is more pessimistic than sales market, with mortgage loan interest rate increases and stricter lending regulations limiting affordability. Tax policy changes and base rate movements are identified as the most critical variables determining future price trajectories.
sections.International Economy: Nongshim, a Korean food company, filed the first tariff refund lawsuit against the Trump administration in US International Trade Court following the Supreme Court's February ruling that tariffs were illegal. The Trump administration suspended preferential tariff benefits for South Africa and Rwanda, threatening up to 10,000 jobs in South Africa where unemployment exceeds 30%. US midterm elections show Democrats leading 52% to Republicans' 45%, with 70% of voters dissatisfied with Trump's inflation response, focusing on tariff policies and energy price impacts. El Nino weather patterns pose significant risk of increasing US inflation by 1 percentage point in 2027 according to San Francisco Federal Reserve research.
sections.AI & Economy: LG CNS opened Korea's K-data center export era by completing the nation's first overseas AI data center construction, with Samsung, SK, and Naver accelerating overseas expansion into booming global AI infrastructure markets. Mercury Communications is establishing a fiber optic cable production base in Mungyeong, Gyeongbuk, targeting the growing demand for high-density multi-core cables from AI data center proliferation. Artificial intelligence financial product recommendations face new transparency and fairness concerns, as UK and other regulatory bodies question whether AI algorithms prioritize affiliated products over consumer optimal choices. Construction equipment exports to the US rebounded for the first time in three years as Doosan Bobcat reports 15% North America sales growth despite interest rate concerns.
sections.Others: Basic pension expenditure is projected to exceed 30 trillion won one year earlier than expected in 2029, with accelerating super-aging driving rapid beneficiary growth and requiring urgent structural reforms. The Lee administration's total government spending through 2030 is forecast to exceed original projections by approximately 80 trillion won due to expanded cash welfare policies and demographic aging impacts. Private loan market concerns are overblown according to ratings agencies, which see AI impact as limited and new investment opportunities emerging in infrastructure-backed lending. Wall Street investors are purchasing loss protection products including put options and credit default swaps against AI investment bubble risks, with some seeking GPU rental rate guarantees.
